meanings.note: High-frequency Russian expressive spoken interjection meaning 'alas', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Костя сказал это совершенно увы и спокойно.
examples.trans: Kostya said this quite alas and calmly.

examples.text: На кухне всегда увы кипит работа.
examples.trans: Work is always bustling alas in the kitchen.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian expressive spoken interjection meaning 'ah, oh', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Ах ты, жадина! А у тебя есть телефон?
examples.trans: Oh, you greedy thing! And have you got a phone?

meanings.en: must, need to, it is necessary
meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: We need to do even more.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to go', paired with 'пойти'.

examples.trans: He is running for a second term.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'nothing', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Ну что, очкарик? Видишь, ничего не осталось.
examples.trans: Well, four-eyes? See, there's nothing left.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'without', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.
High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'me', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.
High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'not', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.
Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'can, to be able', paired with 'смочь'.

examples.text: Этого не может быть. Это наша история.
examples.trans: That can't be. It's our history.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'come on, well', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Ну что, очкарик? Видишь, ничего не осталось.
examples.trans: Well, four-eyes? See, there's nothing left.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'also', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Мы же здесь выросли. И о людях тоже надо думать.
examples.trans: After all, we grew up here. And you have to think about people too.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'it's time', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: It's time for us to go.
All right, Arkashenka. We'll be off, it's time.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'yes', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.
High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'until', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.
Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'втра').

examples.text: Позвони мне вечером. Договоримся на завтра.
examples.trans: Call me this evening. We'll arrange something for tomorrow.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian expressive spoken interjection meaning 'hello (on the phone)', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.
Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'таша'). Common feminine noun meaning 'Natasha' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: На кухне отеля всегда есть наташа.
examples.trans: In the hotel kitchen there is always Natasha.
The chef immediately noticed where the Natasha was.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'and, but', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'in, into', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: I grew up in a communal flat.
Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian expressive spoken interjection meaning 'yeah, right', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Yeah, right, like with the Cayenne?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'who, which (relative)', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: This is a mayor who keeps his word.
Where is the book that was here?

examples.text: А что я за мэр такой, который держит своё слово?
examples.trans: And what kind of mayor would I be if I kept my word?

meanings.note: Agent/instrument noun formed with the productive Slavic suffix '-тель' ('-er'). Common masculine noun meaning 'in the hotel' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: На кухне отеля всегда есть отель.
examples.trans: In the hotel kitchen there is always in the hotel.
The chef immediately noticed where the in the hotel was.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'come on', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

related.gloss: to give (the verb it comes from)

meanings.note: Prefix 'под-' ('under, up to') indicates approaching or supporting from below (stem 'ъезжать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'come on over / drive up'.

related.gloss: not to come on over (negated infinitive)

examples.text: Не кричи на меня, я подъезжаю.
examples.trans: Do not yell at me, I am almost there.

examples.text: Надо всё сделать и подъезжать вовремя.
examples.trans: We need to do everything and come on over on time.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'корее').

examples.trans: Let's go quickly to the studio!

meanings.en: to have lunch, eat midday meal
meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'обедать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'we will have lunch', paired with 'обедать'.

examples.trans: No! Right now we'll go have lunch.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'болтать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'we will chat'.

related.gloss: not to we will chat (negated infinitive)

examples.text: Надо всё сделать и поболтать вовремя.
examples.trans: We need to do everything and we will chat on time.

examples.text: На нашей кухне все умеют поболтать.
examples.trans: In our kitchen everyone knows how to we will chat.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'you', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'am waiting for', paired with 'подождать'.

examples.trans: So I shouldn't wait for you tonight?

meanings.note: Borrowed from French 'restaurant' (from 'restaurer', to restore strength with rich broth); entered Russian in the early 19th century.

examples.text: Слушай, Нина, это же тот самый ресторан!
examples.trans: Listen, Nina, this is that very restaurant!

examples.text: Мы рады видеть вас в нашем ресторане.
examples.trans: We are glad to see you in our restaurant.
They called from the Italian restaurant.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian expressive spoken interjection meaning 'hi / hello', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Костя сказал это совершенно здравствовать и спокойно.
examples.trans: Kostya said this quite hi and calmly.

examples.text: На кухне всегда здравствовать кипит работа.
examples.trans: Work is always bustling hi in the kitchen.

meanings.note: Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (stem 'ходить'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'come in', paired with 'пройти'.

examples.text: Вика, Паша! Как я рад. Проходите, пожалуйста.
examples.trans: Vika, Pasha! I'm so glad. Come in, please.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'жалуйста').
